candidates.change_summary: Replace assignment to owner with assignment to address(0) so transferOwnership always sets owner to the zero address.
Replace assignment to owner with assigning msg.sender, making transferOwnership set owner to the caller instead of the provided newOwner.
Delete the assignment statement so transferOwnership no longer changes the owner.
Replace the require condition to require(msg.sender != owner), inverting the guard so only non-owners can call owner-only functions.
Delete the require statement so onlyOwner modifier no longer enforces ownership (removes the guard), allowing anyone to call transferOwnership.
Insert a revert after the require so the modifier always reverts, preventing transferOwnership from ever completing.
Add a state change that sets owner to the caller inside owned(), causing owner to become msg.sender after calling owned().
Remove the require check from onlyOwner so owned() can be called by anyone, allowing owner to be changed by non-owners if owned() modifies owner.
Removed the onlyOwner modifier from transferOwnership so anyone can call it; this changes who can set owner and therefore final owner value.
Added an extra require that newOwner is not the zero address, preventing transfer to address(0) and changing final owner when such input is used.
Negated the assignment so transferOwnership sets owner to msg.sender instead of the provided newOwner, changing resulting owner.
Changed onlyOwner modifier to require msg.sender != owner, inverting the guard so transferOwnership can be called only by non-owners, changing who can successfully transfer ownership.
